about: Long-premise pilot. Premise = three non-adjacent CS 156 caption chunks of one lecture joined by newlines (P01-P20, built by scripts/s6_long_premise_input.py) or the three retrieved passages of a demo item (Q17, Q18, Q20). Claims written and labelled by one rater (Claude Opus, careful reading of the chunk text); not checked by a human. type A = evidence in one place (ev = chunk number), B = evidence spread over two chunks (ev = both), C = unsupported (alter = a detail changed so the premise contradicts it; partial = one half supported in one chunk, the other half contradicted or absent), R = a real RAGAS statement from the demo run. label 1 = supported, 0 = not supported.

claims.claim: In the perceptron, the threshold is treated as a weight w_0, chosen to be minus the threshold, by introducing an artificial coordinate.
Validation is used after learning to check the solution, and the perceptron learning algorithm starts from random weights.
The perceptron learning algorithm is guaranteed to converge quickly even when the data is not linearly separable.
The final hypothesis g can be any hypothesis from the hypothesis set that the algorithm picks.

Support vector machines prefer one particular solution among those that achieve zero error, and the perceptron learning algorithm is guaranteed to classify all points correctly if the data is linearly separable.
With a stringent tolerance epsilon of 10 to the minus 6, the exponent in the bound stays large, so the probability of a bad event remains very small.
For binary classification, the in-sample error is the frequency of errors and the out-of-sample error is the probability of error.
The Hoeffding inequality bounds the deviation of E_in from E_out by a negative exponential in N, and in the digit example the matrix to invert in linear regression is only 3 by 3.
The professor drew the graph of future income on purpose to show that doing worse in school earns more money.
Learning reduces to two questions: whether the out-of-sample performance is close to the in-sample performance, and whether the in-sample error can be made small.

The noise left over after taking the conditional expected value averages to zero, and the course spends two weeks on the theoretical question of whether out-of-sample performance is close to in-sample performance.
The input distribution P of x plays only a technical role, and the professor gives a formal proof that N pairs of x and y are better than N outputs for one x.
There is no one-size-fits-all method for finding break points.
The number of hypotheses M in the bound is replaced by the growth function, and the final exam is only a way of gauging how well a student has learned the material.
In the credit example, two identical credit applications always lead to the same credit behavior.
B of N and k is defined as the maximum number of dichotomies on N points such that they have a break point k.
The formal proof is in an appendix of six pages, and in the induction step the two summations are merged after renaming the dummy variable.
In the puzzle with three points and break point 2 the answer was 4, and this answer was derived from the formal proof in the appendix.
As a rule of thumb, you need at least 10 times the VC dimension in examples to get reasonable generalization.
Shattering d plus 1 points shows that the VC dimension is at least d plus 1, and if N is greater than the VC dimension then N is a break point.
The rule of 10 times the VC dimension is a mathematical theorem that the professor proves.
Here sigma squared is the variance, or energy, of the noise, which has nothing to do with the variance in the bias-variance analysis.
The derivation starts by adding and subtracting g bar, and g bar may not even be in the hypothesis set.
The exact analysis is specific to linear regression, and bias-variance analysis is a practical tool for model selection because it does not require knowing the target function.
Looking at the data before choosing the model is the most obvious form of data snooping.

Likelihood is the probability of the data given the hypothesis, which is backwards from what we want, and choosing the model after looking at the data forfeits the warranty given by the VC inequality.
In linear regression, the signal s is passed through a hard threshold to give +1 or -1.
Multilayer perceptrons with enough neurons can approximate any function.
Backpropagation is an efficient way to compute the gradient, and for logistic regression initializing the weights to all zeros was fine.
The logistic regression error measure is convex, and for neural networks initializing all the weights to zero is also fine.
Deterministic noise depends on the hypothesis set, while stochastic noise is the same for all hypothesis sets.
At a given point x the deterministic noise is a fixed amount, and in the overfitting example the learners are given 15 points from a 10th-order target.
In a real situation, the energy of the deterministic noise can be measured exactly, just like sigma squared.
Being very rigorous when the main assumption will not hold in the application is described as being penny wise, dollar foolish.
The guideline is to pick a regularizer that prefers smoother hypotheses, and the other approach is purely heuristic, putting the brakes on the minimization of the in-sample error.
The gradient of E_in is orthogonal to the ellipse of constant E_in, and a w for which there is an angle between w and the gradient achieves the constrained minimum.
In the digit example, 500 points are sampled at random for training and the rest are used for testing.

As long as every example appears in the cross-validation estimate exactly once, there is no preference between fold choices as far as bias is concerned, and the nonlinear transform in the digit example is 5th order.
Regularization satisfies the equation relating E_out, E_in and the overfit penalty exactly.
The vector w is perpendicular to the plane w transposed x plus b equals 0.

The distance from x_n to the plane is the absolute value of its projection on the unit vector w hat, and when substituting into the Lagrangian the b term drops out because the sum of alpha_n y_n is zero.
The plane is written as w transposed x plus b equals 0, where b is also known as w_1.
The support vectors are the points whose Lagrange multipliers alpha are greater than zero.
The SVM Lagrangian is passed to a quadratic programming package, and a kernel whose inner product does not converge is not a valid kernel.
Quadratic programming has no problems solving the SVM problem when the number of examples reaches thousands.
Lloyd's algorithm is an iterative algorithm for K-means, and finding the absolute minimum of the K-means problem is NP-hard.
Assuming Gaussian noise in the input x leads to an interpolation that is Gaussian, and Lloyd's algorithm is used as a heuristic for an NP-hard clustering problem.
The support vectors have to be points from the data, and the K-means centers mu are also always points from the data.
The parameters used for normalization must be extracted only from the training set.
With fewer centers than data points, the RBF weights are found with the pseudo-inverse, and an explanation of the data should be as simple as possible but no simpler.
The words 'as simple as possible, but no simpler' are an exact quote that Einstein said in so many words.
Boosting develops its solutions with a view to the fact that they will be blended, which the lecturer calls 'before the fact'.

Blending existing solutions such as those from the Netflix competition is aggregation after the fact, and the probability of D can be ignored when picking between hypotheses because it does not depend on h.

Sampling bias can be compensated when the training distribution is nonzero everywhere, and it can also be compensated when a part of the space has zero probability in training but positive probability in testing.
The logistic function gives exactly one half when the signal s equals zero.
On the learning curves the out-of-sample error goes down as the number of examples grows, and looking at the data before choosing the model forfeits the VC warranty.
With fewer examples, the in-sample error goes up because there is less data to fit.
The lecturer recommends 10-fold cross-validation in practice.
A validation point is an out-of-sample point that was not involved in training, and with 100 validation points a couple of parameters can be estimated.
Each validation error is an unbiased estimate for its own hypothesis, and picking the best of them keeps the estimate unbiased.
The learning rate (eta) determines how much the weights are adjusted at each iteration based on the gradient.
Weight decay pushes weights toward zero to prevent overfitting.
In gradient descent, weight decay effectively shrinks the weights each step.
The shrinking of weights each step is why weight decay is called "decay".
The learning rate scales the gradient update.
Weight decay independently reduces weight magnitude regardless of the gradient.
Linear regression uses squared error.
Linear regression gives a real-valued output.
Logistic regression uses cross-entropy error.
Logistic regression outputs a probability between 0 and 1.
Linear regression should be used for real-valued targets such as deciding a credit line.
Logistic regression should be used for probability estimates such as probability of default.
Increasing the ℓ2 regularization coefficient handicaps the fit.
Handicapping the fit increases bias slightly as a side effect.
Handicapping the fit significantly reduces variance by controlling wild lines and fighting overfitting.
Bias increases while variance decreases.
